summary: Tested the chunked ERP storage and the multi-user merge fix (backend and frontend). BACKEND, 12/12 pass in /app/backend/tests/test_chunked_state.py: login for admin/testing/aaa@amrest.in reads users from chunks; GET /api/erp/state returns data plus version; meta doc has storage=chunked with no 'data' field; the largest chunk is far below 16 MB; the pre-chunk backup exists; collection counts match the backup (grns 368, productionEntries 578, items 1481, POs 337, logs 500). PATCH with the current baseVersion returns 200 and version+1. PATCH with a stale baseVersion returns 409 with detail.version. Calls without a token get 401 and a bad body gets 422. PUT still works. The PATCH round trip leaves data identical. FRONTEND CONCURRENCY, two separate browser contexts on the preview URL: (S1) admin created GRN-2026-380 first, then 'production' (whose tab had loaded before A's save and was not reloaded) saved a Daily Production Entry on JC-2026-030 Finishing. B got PATCH 409, merged, retried and got 200. After 20s and a reload, both contexts show both records and both Activity Log entries, with no duplicates. (S2) Reversed order, production first then GRN: A got 409 then 200, and both records exist. (S3) A deleted GRN-2026-380 while B edited the remarks of the S1 production entry via the Fix modal: B got 409 then 200. The deletion stuck (stock reversed), the edit stuck, and both logs are present. (S4) Two admins (admin and aaa@amrest.in) each created a GRN on the same PO and item at the same time: BOTH GRNs exist, BUT both got the same number GRN-2026-382, and item stock went 7.6 → 8.6 instead of 9.6, so one GRN's stock increment was lost. Single-user flows: GRN edit (invoice#) survives a reload; deleting 3 GRNs via the UI survives a reload; a Settings phone change survives a reload and was reverted. All saves returned PATCH 200 with no page errors. CLEANUP: production entries have no delete in the UI, and the S4 lost update made UI deletion leave the item stock 1 unit low (5.6 vs 6.6). So I took a Mongo snapshot before testing and, after deleting the GRNs via the UI, restored only my own changes through PATCH /api/erp/state: removed the 2 test production entries, put back the JC-2026-030 record, the stock of item bff2a141, grnAudit, and logs (logs restored because the 500-entry cap had pushed out 21 old logs). Before restoring, the diff showed only my test changes (no edits from other users). A final diff against the pre-test snapshot is EMPTY: data is identical and only the version changed (694 → 720).

minor.issue: The commit is not atomic. The version is increased (find_one_and_update) BEFORE the chunks are written by _write_keys. A GET or a 409-merge fetch that runs in that window gets the NEW version with OLD or half-written chunk data. That client can then PATCH successfully with that version and overwrite the other user's just-written collection, which brings back the lost update. Writing large collections (items 1481, logs 500) widens the window. Suggested fixes: write the chunks first under a staging/versioned key and then flip the meta version, or use a Mongo transaction or a per-state lock, and have GET read the meta version after reading the chunks and retry if it changed.

integration_issues.flow: Two users save changes to the SAME record at the same time (lib/merge.ts mergeList)
integration_issues.issue: The merge is record-level, so the local copy of a record replaces the remote copy. When two users change the same item at the same time (two GRNs, GRN + material issue, GRN + SFG production/consumption), one user's currentStock change is lost. Reproduced: 2 concurrent GRNs of 1 unit each raised stock by 1 instead of 2. Deleting those GRNs later then pushes stock below its true value. The same applies to jobCards, purchaseOrders and similar records.

Document numbers are generated in the browser from that tab's possibly outdated list, and the merge does not renumber them. Two concurrent GRNs both got GRN-2026-382. Expect the same for PO, MIS, Job Card, invoice and similar numbers.

The store sets syncStatus and syncError, but no component renders them (grep finds no usage outside lib/store.tsx). The requested check 'sync indicator shows connected' therefore cannot be checked in the UI: there is no indicator. Users get no warning when a save fails.

integration_issues.flow: Save on tab close or logout (patchRemoteDBFinal)
integration_issues.issue: This is fire-and-forget. If it gets a 409, the unsaved changes are silently dropped with no merge or retry. Also, flushSave gives up after 6 conflict attempts and still sets status to 'connected'.

action_items: HIGH: Make concurrent changes to the same record safe for numeric stock fields. Either apply local deltas in merge3 (remote + (local - base) for currentStock and similar counters) or move stock changes to the server using $inc. Today 2 concurrent GRNs on one item lose one increment.
HIGH: Avoid duplicate document numbers under concurrency. After a 409 merge, renumber any locally added records whose number clashes with a remote one, or have the server allocate numbers.
MEDIUM: Make _commit atomic (write chunks first, then bump the version, or use a transaction or lock) so a reader never sees the new version with old data.
MEDIUM: Show syncStatus and syncError in the header (connected/syncing/error), and do not report 'connected' when flushSave gives up with unsaved changes.
LOW: Handle a 409 for the final save on unload/logout (for example, keep the pending changes in localStorage and retry on the next load).
LOW: Format the Dashboard donut numbers to 2 decimals.

However, lists of primitives or non-id objects fall back to 'local wins', which overwrites the remote value. That is fine for the settings arrays edited by one admin, but note it.
_ensure_chunked runs on every login and every GET. It is cheap (meta find_one) but could be cached once it reports 'chunked'.
The pre-chunk backup (about 14 MB) is kept in erp_state_backup. This is fine, but document a retention plan.
Logs are capped at 500 in each client after a merge. Concurrent heavy activity pushes old logs out faster, which is expected.

rca of the issue: The original bug (records visible in the Activity Log but missing from GRN/Production) is FIXED for the reported case, where different users edit different collections or different records. A stale tab now gets a 409, merges by record id, and keeps the other user's records. A remaining variant: two users changing the SAME record (an item's currentStock) at the same time. The merge keeps the whole record from the side that saved last, so one change is lost. Reproduce by having two contexts each GRN 1 unit of the same item on PO-2026-365, 2.5s apart: stock rises by +1 only and both GRNs are numbered GRN-2026-382. Fix by merging numeric counters by delta or moving stock changes to the server, and by renumbering clashing document numbers after a merge.
